title: Seed replay rewrites unchanged rows on every boot: `seedValueEquals` compares time and ISO-datetime strings literally, so `09:15` vs `09:15:00` and `…Z` vs `….000Z` bump `updated_at` (5 showcase rows per restart)
body:
Filing gate: ① — product defect with a named location and a reproduction (QA-measured).

Path: platform-core.seed-integrity (priority P0) — acceptance[3] states "upsert with externalId no-ops on unchanged rows"; its count oracle cannot see this, so the clause scored pass while its parenthetical is violated (tri-state ②: the item asserts the capability, its steps do not reach the path).
Type: Bug (prefilled — violates `isNoOpReplay`'s own documented behaviour, quoted below)
QA-source: #24557 · platform-core.seed-integrity · acceptance[3]

reach: measured once on a public boot — two `objectstack dev` boots of the stock showcase against the same file DB: 5 seeded rows whose seed values are unchanged get a new `updated_at` on the second boot (read via `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo`, `/showcase_invoice_line`, `/showcase_invoice`), at framework 5b14b7f3.

## What happens

Every dev-server restart / package re-publish re-writes seeded rows whose declared values did not change, whenever the seed spells a **time** or **datetime** value differently from the driver's stored form. On stock showcase that is 5 rows per boot: "Specimen — Full" (field zoo), the invoice lines "INV-1001 · Consulting hours" and "INV-1004 · Consulting hours", and their parent invoices INV-1001 and INV-1004. Counts and ids are unchanged (no duplication); `updated_at` is bumped, lifecycle validation re-runs, and history tracking can log a phantom edit — exactly what the no-op skip exists to prevent.

Control: "Specimen — Minimal", authored with a full `'09:05:30'`, does not churn.

## Reproduction

1. Boot showcase fresh: `OS_PORT=P objectstack dev --seed-admin -p P -d file:RUN/data.db` (banner: `Seeds: com.example.showcase 132 rows`).
2. Snapshot `id, updated_at` of every seeded object (`GET /api/v1/data/OBJECT?$top=200`).
3. Stop; boot again against the SAME file DB; snapshot again.
4. expected: all 132 rows byte-identical including `updated_at` (the replay is a no-op). actual: counts and ids identical, 5 rows carry a new `updated_at`.

## Mechanism

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`, `isNoOpReplay` → `seedValueEquals`: dates are normalised only when one side is a `Date` instance; ISO strings and time strings fall through to `String(a) === String(b)`. So the seed's `'09:15'` ≠ stored `'09:15:00'`, and `'…T…Z'` ≠ stored `'….000Z'`, and the row is rewritten.

The method's own docblock declares the intended behaviour: "When nothing the seed declares actually differs, rewriting the row is pure churn: `updated_at` gets bumped every boot, lifecycle validation re-runs …, and history tracking logs a phantom edit. Skip those." Its "any doubt reads as changed" escape covers unparseable values, not two spellings of the same instant.

Suggested permanent test: seed-mode-matrix's replay negative with a time and a datetime field on the scratch object.

## Filing-gate answers

- Category: ① (finding class (a): reproducible defect; reach measured above).
- Acting reader: `domain:engine` seat dev — a fix in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts` (`seedValueEquals`: normalise ISO datetime and time-of-day strings by field type before comparing) plus a replay pin.
- Duplicate search (open AND closed), objectstack: "seed replay rewrites unchanged rows updated_at bumped every boot isNoOpReplay time datetime format" → 6 hits (#21646, #15302, #9633, #3994, #3433, #3434 — none this defect; #3994 is the adjacent time-write normalisation).
